verses.text: There was a man named Micah who lived in the hill country of Ephraim.

He said to his mother, "Someone took eleven hundred pieces of silver from you, and I heard you curse the thief. Well, I have the silver. I took it." Then his mother said, "May the LORD bless you, my son!"

When he gave the eleven hundred pieces of silver back to his mother, she said, "I am giving this silver to the LORD for my son, to make a carved idol covered with silver. So now I give it back to you."
After he gave the silver back to his mother, she took two hundred pieces of it to a silversmith, who used it to make the idol. It was put in Micah's house.
Micah had a shrine, and he made an ephod and some household gods. He set apart one of his sons to be his priest.
In those days Israel had no king. Everyone did whatever they thought was right.
A young Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, from the clan of Judah, had been living there.
He left Bethlehem in Judah to look for another place to live. On his way he came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim.
Micah asked him, "Where are you from?" He answered, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I am looking for a place to stay."
Then Micah said to him, "Live with me and be my father and priest. I will give you ten pieces of silver a year, a set of clothes, and your food." So the Levite went in.
The Levite agreed to live with him, and the young man became like one of his sons.
Then Micah set apart the Levite, and the young man became his priest and lived in his house.
And Micah said, "Now I know that the LORD will be good to me, because this Levite has become my priest."
